title: Silicon Dioxide Nanofertilizers Improve Physiological Performance and Yield of Three Pepper Hybrids (Capsicum annuum L.) Under Field Conditions
content: In order to assess the effect of silicon dioxide nanofertilizers (NFs-SiO2) on physiological and agronomic traits in three bell pepper hybrids –Salvador, H1; Zapata, H2 and Cortes, H3– grown in the field, a randomized block design trial was conducted in which the leaves were sprayed with NFs-SiO₂ (400 mg L⁻¹) and photosynthesis (A), transpiration (E), stomatal conductance (gs), water use efficiency (WUE), chlorophyll index (SPAD), leaf area index (LAI) and water potential (Y) were evaluated in the field at 28 and 42 days after the first spray; agronomic variables (height, stem diameter, number of leaves, number of branches, number of flowers, number of fruits, and yield) were assessed. Sprayed NFs-SiO₂ resulted in significant differences in gas exchange; plants treated with NFs-SiO₂ exhibited lower A, E, and gs values, which led to higher values of WUE and Y in the hybrids studied compared to the controls. Leaf sprayed with NFs-SiO₂ had a positive effect on LAI, without no changes in chlorophyll index. Hybrids H2 and H3 treated with NFs-SiO2 showed increases of 16.8% in height, and 18.8% in stem diameter; 18.5% in the number of leaves, and 11.7 % in the number of branches. A significant increase in yield of 38.9%, 53.2%, and 55.2% was observed in H1, H2, and H3, respectively, when sprayed with NFs-SiO2 compared to the controls. It was concluded that the use of NFs-SiO₂ may represent a highly beneficial technology for bell pepper cultivation under field conditions and has a distinct physiological and yield-enhancing effect depending on the hybrid.
